_readme: Permanent triage ledger for App/parse_prices.py's Cattelan-format review_flags mechanism (a block the parser declined to guess at rather than risk parsing wrong). Every product name that has EVER appeared in a review flag must have an entry here recording what was found. This is the tracked follow-up list that check_orphaned_flags.ts enforces -- a fresh flag on a product not listed here fails the build, forcing triage to happen instead of being silently forgotten (the exact bug found 2026-08-06: SAN MARCO/BLUEBELL/NAHUN/REGATA/LAVANDER were flagged but never followed up, and the app kept serving accessory-only data for them for an unknown period). Add a brand's product_name to CATTELAN_FORMAT_BRANDS in check_orphaned_flags.ts when a new brand (e.g. Bonaldo) starts using --format cattelan, so its flags get tracked from day one.

_status_meaning.real_gap: The flagged block was a genuine, entirely-missing price table. Fixed by hand-transcribing it into manual_additions.json (verified against the real page image, complete row set including any pre-existing correct rows since merge_manual_additions.py replaces the whole product).
_status_meaning.partial: The main price data was already correct; only a smaller secondary table (e.g. a Cavo aggiuntivo/Accessori row) was missing. Fixed the same way as real_gap, just a smaller row set.
_status_meaning.false_alarm: Checked the raw source text (and page image where the text alone was ambiguous) and confirmed prices.json already has the complete, correct data. The flag was about some other non-price element on the page, or a row count that looked suspicious but was correct. Nothing added to manual_additions.json.
_status_meaning.known_gap: Batch-categorized (not individually page-verified like real_gap/partial/false_alarm) into one of a small set of documented root-cause buckets -- used for Bonaldo's initial 197-product seeding on 2026-08-07, where per-product page-image verification the way Cattelan's SAN MARCO etc. got would have been a multi-session effort on its own. Every instance is a SAFE flag (parser returns zero rows / skips the ambiguous row rather than guessing -- never silently wrong). Does not require a manual_additions.json entry. A future dedicated cleanup pass should convert these to real_gap/partial/false_alarm per product as each bucket gets addressed (see bonaldo_index_and_structure memory for the per-bucket game plan).

Common pattern: a single stray accessory/sub-component code (bed-base cover panel codes ZL00X/ZT01X, carpet shade codes TAPPJTPXX, chair-leg-finish codes EXCLUSIVE/TERRA, cushion codes MIDI/CLOUD) sitting on a page whose price-table shape this pass did not verify in depth. A future dedicated pass should convert these to real_gap/partial/false_alarm per product, same as the existing Bonaldo/Cattelan buckets. Codes flagged on this product: ONLIA1A00. ALSO TRACKED (found 2026-08-18, corrupted source data, not a matching-logic bug): 12 rows for On Line have a merged/corrupted model_variant literally stored as "3-er maxi central element                              Mini terminal element" (two adjacent variant-column headers glued into one string with a long run of raw whitespace between them), and their fabric_tier values are similarly corrupted with raw dot-leader table text bleeding in verbatim, e.g. "Customer's fabric................... 4.598,00 €        Customer's fabric" (code ONLIC300M, page 214). Root cause: the PDF table extraction merged two adjacent table columns ('3-er maxi central element' and 'Mini terminal element' are two DIFFERENT, legitimate On Line variants -- 'Mini terminal element' does not otherwise appear as its own distinct model_variant anywhere in On Line's data, meaning its whole column may have been swallowed into this one) without a correct column boundary, and let dot-leader formatting artifacts (table-of-contents-style '....' price leaders) leak into the extracted fabric_tier text instead of being stripped. Confirmed pre-existing: present in prices.json before tonight's session (verified via direct read of the source file, independent of any runtime code). Was previously unreachable/never surfaced to a user because no prior query happened to select this specific variant; became visible only after tonight's separate matching-logic fix (coverage-ratio tie-break in lookupForProduct) started resolving 'on line 3er...'-style queries more precisely -- precision surfaced a pre-existing data defect, did not create one. Real fix needs the PDF table-extraction column-boundary logic (App/parse_prices.py, Ditre's Shape 1/Shape 2 handling) reviewed for this specific page/table shape (p.214) and likely a re-scan for the same merged-column pattern elsewhere in Ditre's data -- deliberately not attempted this session, same as the range-dims item below. ALSO TRACKED: TRACKED BUG (not a per-product data gap): _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE (App/parse_prices.py) is "^\s*(?:W\s*)?[\d.,]+\s*cm" -- it requires a SINGLE numeric value before "cm" and does not match RANGE-format dims printed as "W 200-230cm" (a hyphenated low-high range, not one number). Root cause chain: _ditre_scan_sku_block walks forward from a code-header line looking for the first line whose column-0 chunk matches _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE, to know where the real price rows start. When the dims line uses range format, this match never succeeds, so the walk silently continues PAST the SKU's own real dims/price content, through the whole price grid, and into the NEXT SKU header/block entirely -- confirmed exact repro: Blum's BLUMD2000 (header text/blum.txt line 89) never finds its own dims line 99 ("W 200-230cmD 90-113cm"), the scan overruns to line 125+ and BLUMD2000 ends up carrying BLUMU1000's ("Footstool", an unrelated later SKU) price values instead of its own. Confirmed PRE-EXISTING: present in the catalog before any of this session's Ditre work (verified directly against a pre-session prices.json snapshot). Currently masked, not silently wrong in production: the misattributed values conflict with the SKU's OTHER real occurrences elsewhere in the text, so they land in the ambiguous-price safety net (shown as "can't confirm, view the page" rather than a false-confident wrong number) -- confirmed on BLUMD2000's "Customer's fabric" tier (3 conflicting values, all ambiguous=true, one of them the misattributed one). SEVERITY RISK: this safety net is fragile, not a real fix -- it depends on there being enough OTHER conflicting occurrences of the same code to keep the ambiguous count above 1. A same-session attempt at a DIFFERENT fix (reversible-dual-SKU-pair header recognition, see the "bare-code-next-to-reversible-pair" item) reduced accumulated-duplicate counts broadly enough that BLUMD2000's conflict count would have dropped to a single, no-longer-ambiguous, CONFIDENTLY WRONG value -- caught before shipping, that fix was reverted specifically because of this interaction, not because it was wrong on its own. Any future fix that reduces duplicate/repeat scanning needs to re-check this risk first. Scope, found via a catalog-wide text search for the range-dims pattern (\d+-\d+\s*cm), NOT individually verified product-by-product beyond Blum: Atlantis, Bepop, Blum (confirmed), Isla (Sofa), Isla slim, Kris Low, Kris Mix Low, Krisby (Sofa), Krisby low, Krisby mix, Krisby mix low, Melville (Sofa), On Line, On Line Plain, Sanders, Urban 2.0 (Sofa) -- 16 products total. Real fix needs _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE (and likely _DITRE_DIMS_WD_VALUES_RE) extended to accept a hyphenated range and decide which value (low/high/both) represents the size, verified against real rendered pages -- deliberately not attempted this session. ALSO TRACKED (found 2026-08-18, chat-matching logic gap, not a data gap -- logged, NOT fixed, per explicit instruction to stop live-patching for the night): (1) "give all online 2er price" surfaces an unexpected extra variant, "2-er central element", alongside the intended "2-er sofa". Root cause: the same session's final tied-variant tie-break redesign (commit bb5cd01) deliberately broadens ties for a bare shared word with no other distinguishing text (needed and verified correct for "give online sofa price" tying all 6 real sofa variants) -- but a bare DIGIT-WORD alone ("2er", with no other real word in the query at all) gets the exact same broadening treatment, and every On Line variant starting with "2-er" ties together regardless of category ("2-er sofa" and "2-er central element" share only the digit "2", nothing else in common). This is a direct, understood side effect of tonight's tie-break design, not a mystery -- it just wasn't caught by tonight's verification battery, which tested bare "3er"/"2er" as an internal reconstruction detail (inside the elision feature) but never as a directly-typed user query in its own right. (2) "give online 3er category u, A and leather vip" (a 3-clause tier list combining a comma AND "and") does not resolve to the 3 specific requested tier prices -- it returns a broad multi-match spanning 4 different "3-er ..." variants (3-er sofa, 3-er maxi sofa, 3-er extra sofa, 3-er central element) x the 3 correctly-resolved tiers (Category A, Category U, Leather Vip) = 12 rows, instead of narrowing to just "3-er sofa"'s 3 rows. Root cause: the comma+"and" tier-list parsing itself works correctly (all 3 tiers resolve right) -- the failure is the SAME bare-digit-word broadening as (1): once the 3 tier words are correctly consumed as tier signal (not variant signal), "3er" is the only remaining variant-distinguishing text in the query, and it ties across the whole "3-er family" the same way bare "3er" always does post-bb5cd01, rather than narrowing to a single variant. RECOMMENDATION: do not live-patch either of these further -- see project memory (tiedvariant_coverage_ratio_fix.md, and a new dedicated memory entry) recommending a proper up-front test battery covering every Ditre chat-matching pattern found broken this session (multi-clause and/comma combinations, elision, digit-prefixed variants, typo tolerance), designed and verified together before any further live patching -- reactive single-query fixes at this depth already caused 2 real regressions tonight (the Krisby tie and the elision-regex interaction), both caught only because a combined battery was insisted on before landing. RESOLVED 2026-08-19 (dedicated hardening session, battery-first discipline): the reversed-clause-order elision silent-drop ("3er maxi and 3er all price" / "3er all and 3er maxi price" -- a real bug found via this session's own battery, not previously reported) is fixed via a symmetric mirror fallback in resolveProductQuery (variantA-resolved-but-not-variantB is now handled the same way the reverse was already handled). The 2 previously-logged bare-digit-word broadening findings ("give all online 2er price" pulling in "2-er central element"; the 3-clause tier-list case tying the whole "3-er..." family) were investigated in depth and are KEPT AS-IS deliberately, not rescored: they are the correct, safe, honest behavior per this project's standing philosophy (never confidently narrow to a single wrong answer when the query truly contains no distinguishing signal beyond a shared capacity digit -- these ARE 2-4 real, structurally different products that only share that digit). What changed instead: full_price_grid/multiple_options responses now explicitly name every distinct model_variant included whenever 2+ remain tied, so the ambiguity is visible in the message text rather than silently implied by a generic product-name label. Verified via a new 34-case dedicated battery (App/regression/check_ditre_matching.ts, wired into regression:full) covering both gaps, every prior-session regression guardrail, and new typo/multi-clause/elision-order variations -- 32/32 hard-assertion cases pass, 2 observational (documented, not asserted: 2-word elision modifiers, a non-canonical "yess" confirmation typo).

Freedom 2.0 sofa-bed armrests S.note: PERMANENT known_gap (same standard as every other brand's accepted triage items, e.g. Bonaldo's Geometric Table 400/Mellow 400) -- not a pending "next session" item. Root cause precisely diagnosed: the "Surcharge for Move mechanism" note is not printed in any of its block's real SKU columns -- it starts at a character position INSIDE the range of the block's own last-but-one SKU column, a few characters before that column's right edge (confirmed exact repro: freedom_20_sofa-bed_armrests_s.txt line 144, "Surcharge for Move" starts at character 216, inside column D3T0M's [144,220) range). This truncates the label mid-word for that column and bleeds the remainder into the NEXT column, concatenated with an unrelated adjacent note ("Optional bed-base cover: see dedicated section"). Safe to leave permanently unfixed: the row is silently MISSING, never silently wrong -- no fabricated or misattributed price shows in its place, and no review_flag fires for it (each product has other, correctly-captured rows for the same code, so it never crosses the 0-rows-for-a-code threshold that would flag it). Atlantis.note: TRACKED BUG (not a per-product data gap): _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE (App/parse_prices.py) is "^\s*(?:W\s*)?[\d.,]+\s*cm" -- it requires a SINGLE numeric value before "cm" and does not match RANGE-format dims printed as "W 200-230cm" (a hyphenated low-high range, not one number). Root cause chain: _ditre_scan_sku_block walks forward from a code-header line looking for the first line whose column-0 chunk matches _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE, to know where the real price rows start. When the dims line uses range format, this match never succeeds, so the walk silently continues PAST the SKU's own real dims/price content, through the whole price grid, and into the NEXT SKU header/block entirely -- confirmed exact repro: Blum's BLUMD2000 (header text/blum.txt line 89) never finds its own dims line 99 ("W 200-230cmD 90-113cm"), the scan overruns to line 125+ and BLUMD2000 ends up carrying BLUMU1000's ("Footstool", an unrelated later SKU) price values instead of its own. Confirmed PRE-EXISTING: present in the catalog before any of this session's Ditre work (verified directly against a pre-session prices.json snapshot). Currently masked, not silently wrong in production: the misattributed values conflict with the SKU's OTHER real occurrences elsewhere in the text, so they land in the ambiguous-price safety net (shown as "can't confirm, view the page" rather than a false-confident wrong number) -- confirmed on BLUMD2000's "Customer's fabric" tier (3 conflicting values, all ambiguous=true, one of them the misattributed one). SEVERITY RISK: this safety net is fragile, not a real fix -- it depends on there being enough OTHER conflicting occurrences of the same code to keep the ambiguous count above 1. A same-session attempt at a DIFFERENT fix (reversible-dual-SKU-pair header recognition, see the "bare-code-next-to-reversible-pair" item) reduced accumulated-duplicate counts broadly enough that BLUMD2000's conflict count would have dropped to a single, no-longer-ambiguous, CONFIDENTLY WRONG value -- caught before shipping, that fix was reverted specifically because of this interaction, not because it was wrong on its own. Any future fix that reduces duplicate/repeat scanning needs to re-check this risk first. Scope, found via a catalog-wide text search for the range-dims pattern (\d+-\d+\s*cm), NOT individually verified product-by-product beyond Blum: Atlantis, Bepop, Blum (confirmed), Isla (Sofa), Isla slim, Kris Low, Kris Mix Low, Krisby (Sofa), Krisby low, Krisby mix, Krisby mix low, Melville (Sofa), On Line, On Line Plain, Sanders, Urban 2.0 (Sofa) -- 16 products total. Real fix needs _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE (and likely _DITRE_DIMS_WD_VALUES_RE) extended to accept a hyphenated range and decide which value (low/high/both) represents the size, verified against real rendered pages -- deliberately not attempted this session.

When the dims line uses range format, this match never succeeds, so the walk silently continues PAST the SKU's own real dims/price content, through the whole price grid, and into the NEXT SKU header/block entirely -- confirmed exact repro: Blum's BLUMD2000 (header text/blum.txt line 89) never finds its own dims line 99 ("W 200-230cmD 90-113cm"), the scan overruns to line 125+ and BLUMD2000 ends up carrying BLUMU1000's ("Footstool", an unrelated later SKU) price values instead of its own. Confirmed PRE-EXISTING: present in the catalog before any of this session's Ditre work (verified directly against a pre-session prices.json snapshot). Currently masked, not silently wrong in production: the misattributed values conflict with the SKU's OTHER real occurrences elsewhere in the text, so they land in the ambiguous-price safety net (shown as "can't confirm, view the page" rather than a false-confident wrong number) -- confirmed on BLUMD2000's "Customer's fabric" tier (3 conflicting values, all ambiguous=true, one of them the misattributed one). SEVERITY RISK: this safety net is fragile, not a real fix -- it depends on there being enough OTHER conflicting occurrences of the same code to keep the ambiguous count above 1. A same-session attempt at a DIFFERENT fix (reversible-dual-SKU-pair header recognition, see the "bare-code-next-to-reversible-pair" item) reduced accumulated-duplicate counts broadly enough that BLUMD2000's conflict count would have dropped to a single, no-longer-ambiguous, CONFIDENTLY WRONG value -- caught before shipping, that fix was reverted specifically because of this interaction, not because it was wrong on its own. Any future fix that reduces duplicate/repeat scanning needs to re-check this risk first. Scope, found via a catalog-wide text search for the range-dims pattern (\d+-\d+\s*cm), NOT individually verified product-by-product beyond Blum: Atlantis, Bepop, Blum (confirmed), Isla (Sofa), Isla slim, Kris Low, Kris Mix Low, Krisby (Sofa), Krisby low, Krisby mix, Krisby mix low, Melville (Sofa), On Line, On Line Plain, Sanders, Urban 2.0 (Sofa) -- 16 products total. Real fix needs _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE (and likely _DITRE_DIMS_WD_VALUES_RE) extended to accept a hyphenated range and decide which value (low/high/both) represents the size, verified against real rendered pages -- deliberately not attempted this session.

Stone-in.note: Pre-existing bug, confirmed NOT caused by this session's excludeUnrelatedAndClause/qWords digit-signal fixes (identical reproduction on the pre-session baseline, commit 89a4ac5, before either fix landed). Root cause: checkFamilyAmbiguity (App/server/catalogChat.ts) treats 'Stone-in' and 'Stone-out outdoor' as a reciprocal 1-shared-leading-token family (both tokenize via tokenizeLoose to ['stone',...], sharing only 'stone' -- the session-5 Puppet-fix extension's own scope). To resolve which family member a query means, it strips CONVERSATIONAL_FILLER_WORDS from the query text first -- but 'in' has been in that list since before this session, and 'in' is ALSO Stone-in's own literal distinguishing suffix (tokenizeLoose splits the hyphen: ['stone','in']). A query naming the product by its own exact name ('give me all prices for Stone-in') has its own distinguishing 'in' token stripped as filler before the satisfied-member check runs, so NEITHER family member ends up satisfied, and it falls through to clarify_product instead of resolving directly. Confirmed deterministic (not LLM-flaky): reproduces identically across repeated direct calls to checkFamilyAmbiguity itself, only visible in the live regression report when the LLM path happens to confidently resolve the product name first (this session's earlier regression runs did not trigger it, likely LLM-path variance in which queries got real calls vs. the deterministic fallback -- which resolves both products correctly, since answer()'s own topMatches/maximal path never calls checkFamilyAmbiguity at all). Real, fixable root cause identified (a word in CONVERSATIONAL_FILLER_WORDS should not be treated as filler when it is ALSO the chosen family member's own distinguishing suffix) -- not a case of genuinely unparseable/unfixable data.
